title: China's AI chipmakers target 3D packaging, optical interconnects and software ecosystems
snippet: China's domestic AI chipmakers are shifting their competitive focus from individual GPU performance to system-level integration as AI models grow increasingly complex. Three priorities—3D packaging for greater power efficiency, optical interconnects for faster data transmission, and open software ecosystems for easier adoption—will determine whether Chinese GPUs can advance from standalone accelerators to large-scale AI computing clusters.

title: GlobalFoundries revives 7nm-class ambitions with an EUV-free FD-SOI bet on physical AI
snippet: GlobalFoundries' plan to build a 7nm-class chip process in Dresden without extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography tests how a second-tier foundry can stay relevant while TSMC holds most of the AI data center market. Instead of competing on transistor size, GF is competing on integration, power efficiency, and location, and it is making European supply security part of its pitch.

title: Applied Materials lifts 2030 margin goals, but a missing industry forecast sends a disappointing signal
snippet: Applied Materials used its investor day to argue that AI will let it outgrow the chip equipment market through 2030. Investors, however, focused on what the company left out: a forecast for wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending, the industry-wide figure that drives demand for its tools.

title: Analysis: China's EV rebate cut pushes exporters from volume to value
snippet: China's planned cut to export tax rebates for new energy vehicles could ripple through global auto markets, intensifying pressure on low-cost exporters while reshaping trade tensions with Europe. The move signals a wider rollback of industry support and may accelerate consolidation among weaker carmakers and raise prices for some overseas buyers.

title: NTT Data, Anthropic negotiate Japan data center with up to 500MW
snippet: NTT Data and Anthropic are in final-stage negotiations to develop a data center in Osaka, Japan, with power capacity of up to 500MW, according to Nikkei. The project would be Anthropic's first dedicated data center in Japan and one of the country's largest facilities, supporting the AI model developer's expanding infrastructure requirements.

title: Apple COO visits Foxconn as iPhone Duo production ramps up
snippet: Days before preorders open for Apple's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, Apple Chief Operating Officer Sabih Khan visited China to inspect its supply chain. On October 11, Khan and Foxconn rotating CEO Michael Chiang toured Foxconn's Zhengzhou technology park in Henan, focusing on iPhone Duo production, iPhone 18 Pro rear-camera modules, anodizing for exterior midframes, and chip-level surface-sputtering manufacturing.

title: TSMC-GF interposer deal reshapes US AI supply chain, from CoWoS to HBM
snippet: GlobalFoundries (GF) and TSMC have reached a manufacturing agreement to establish a US-based supply source for silicon interposers supporting TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging ecosystem. The US$2 billion, five-year agreement will expand advanced packaging capacity and support growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) technologies.

title: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger sees hardware renaissance in memory, optical interconnects
snippet: As AI reshapes the global computing landscape, former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger said AI is making chip design easier, while physical bottlenecks in manufacturing, memory, and energy are driving an unprecedented hardware renaissance. Gelsinger recently joined a16z's latest interview program, where he discussed chip design, memory innovation, and optical interconnects with Raghu Raghuram and Guido Appenzeller.

title: Shield AI delivers first V-BAT drone to Taiwan Coast Guard
snippet: US defense technology company Shield AI has delivered its first V-BAT vertical takeoff and landing unmanned aircraft to Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration after winning a contract. The company expects to deliver 12 aircraft in the coming months and will work with Taiwan's Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) to support logistics, maintenance, training, autonomous systems integration, deployment, and scaled operations in Taiwan.

title: Starlink moves from satellite overlay to mobile challenger as SpaceX builds hybrid network
snippet: From constellation-scale satellite deployment to terrestrial network expansion, SpaceX is deepening Starlink's reach across the connectivity stack. The latest moves suggest the company is no longer positioning direct-to-device (D2D) merely as a way to fill cellular dead zones, but as a foundation for a broader hybrid mobile network capable of competing more directly with US carriers.

title: AI memory boom pushes smartphone market into premium-first reset
snippet: While the rapid advancement of AI has driven steadily growing investment in large-scale infrastructure, one of its downstream effects is becoming increasingly visible in the memory sector, where supply has tightened as vendors prioritize higher-margin AI workloads.

title: PMIC vendors diverge as PC exposure drives revenue gap
snippet: Taiwanese power management IC (PMIC) vendors reported their September and third-quarter 2026 revenue, with results diverging as PC exposure widened the performance gap. Global Mixed-mode Technology and Leadtrend posted both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year growth in the third quarter, while Anpec Electronics and uPI Semiconductor reported declines from the previous quarter, amid weak PC supply-chain demand.

title: Huawei accelerates ASEAN data center hardware supply as Kunpeng chip exports surge
snippet: Leveraging Singapore as its regional hub, Huawei has expanded hardware deployments, such as servers, across data centers in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region. Following the US revocation of certain Intel chip export licenses to Huawei in 2024, the Chinese tech giant has aggressively adopted its proprietary Kunpeng chipsets, resulting in a dramatic increase in Kunpeng shipments to ASEAN data centers and telecom base stations, according to DIGITIMES Intelligence.

title: Smartphone costs surge as brands take divergent action
snippet: Memory prices have surged 4–5x in recent years, and smartphone brands' efforts to pass those costs on to consumers have already hurt sales of new devices in 2026. With large-scale AI deployments continuing to drive strong demand, the memory shortage is expected to persist, putting further pressure on smartphone prices in 2027.

title: Taiwan FPCB maker CMI targets flat 2026 revenue despite memory, CPU shortages hitting notebook demand
snippet: Flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) manufacturer Complex Micro Interconnection (CMI) reported September 2026 revenue of NT$163 million (≈ US$5.1 million), down 15.43% year-on-year, bringing consolidated revenue for the first nine months to NT$1.718 billion, a decline of 7.52%. The company attributed the weaker September performance to memory and CPU shortages, which dampened customer orders for components used in commercial and consumer notebooks.

title: China's wafer-scale graphene breakthrough brings quantum rectifiers closer to semiconductor integration
snippet: Chinese researchers have demonstrated wafer-scale graphene quantum rectifiers that convert weak radio-frequency signals into DC electricity at room temperature without an external magnetic field. title: AP Memory completes US$415.5M GDR offering, boosts three product lines
snippet: Memory IC design house AP Memory Technology has successfully priced its global depositary receipt (GDR) offering, raising a total of US$415.5 million. The GDRs were priced at US$56.15 per unit, representing approximately NT$897.61 per common share based on an exchange rate of NT$31.972 per US dollar. Scheduled to list on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange on October 15, the proceeds will be used to bolster working capital and satisfy foreign-currency raw material procurement needs.

title: Chinese automakers face three hidden barriers in European expansion
snippet: China-based automakers are mounting an aggressive push into Europe, enjoying rapid early momentum. However, supply chain analysts note that the ultra-fast development model perfected in their domestic market cannot be seamlessly replicated in Europe. Currently, at least three hidden barriers test their cross-border adaptability.

title: Apple's new home devices tie Siri AI to subscriptions and newer iPhones
snippet: The smart home hardware Apple unveiled on October 13 is priced as premium equipment, but the fine print points to two larger goals. The first is to put Siri AI, Apple's new generative assistant, on more screens and speakers around the home. The second is to turn those devices into a channel for recurring services revenue. Many of the most capable features also require a recent iPhone.

title: LGES diversifies ESS equipment suppliers after Daejin Machinery default, court rehabilitation
snippet: LG Energy Solution (LGES) is reportedly restructuring its energy storage system (ESS) battery equipment supply chain after major partner Daejin Machinery entered financial difficulties and began court-led rehabilitation proceedings. LGES is transferring some orders to existing equipment suppliers while seeking new partners to reduce the risk of supply disruptions.

title: China’s NEV export rebate cut puts budget EV makers under margin pressure
snippet: China will reduce its export tax rebate for new energy vehicles (NEVs) from 13% to 9% on April 1, 2027, increasing cost pressure on automakers, particularly those selling lower-priced models with thin profit margins. The Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration announced the four-percentage-point reduction on October 12.

title: Apple launches HomeView display, rebuilding home lineup around Siri AI
snippet: Apple is betting that its new Siri AI assistant can revive a business in which, according to Reuters, the company "has tinkered for a decade without major success." At its "Welcome Home" launch in New York on October 13, 2026, Apple introduced HomeView, a new smart display, alongside a new HomePod mini, a faster Apple TV 4K, and a range of cameras, a smart lock, and thermostats made by LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

title: MiTAC spotlights liquid cooling, open platforms for AI infrastructure
snippet: MiTAC Computing Technology featured a comprehensive suite of full-stack AI infrastructure at the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit in San Jose, California, centered around the theme "Scaling Open AI Infra with Full-Stack Innovation." The company demonstrated integrated solutions spanning compute, storage, liquid-cooled servers, firmware, operating systems, and management software.

title: TSMC, Intel, Samsung seek to break AI chipmaking's next barrier through early technology integration
snippet: Senior executives from TSMC, Intel, and Samsung Electronics outlined the growing challenges of AI chip development, spanning advanced semiconductor processes, 3D integration, and research models, at the October 12 opening of Applied Materials' Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center in the US.

title: Geely enters Canada, plans first vehicles for 2027
snippet: China's Geely has officially entered the Canadian market and plans to launch its first vehicles there in 2027, expanding its North American footprint. Geely has completed its Canadian corporate registration and begun operations while building local sales and after-sales service networks.

title: TCC wins approval for Europe listing plan
snippet: TCC Group Holdings (TCC) shareholders approved a plan on October 13 for subsidiary Cimpor International Holdings to pursue an initial public offering (IPO) and listing on a European securities market. The resolution received 4,287,569,701 votes in favor, representing 94.74% of voting rights represented at the vote, as the company sought to create a new funding channel for its European operations while maintaining Taiwan-based control of the business.

title: SEMICON West makes three-year commitment to Phoenix, home to over US$200B in chip investment
snippet: SEMI announced at a media event during SEMICON West 2026 that the exhibition will move to Phoenix, Arizona, in 2027 and shift to a spring schedule. SEMI Americas President Joe Stockunas confirmed at a pre-show press conference that the organization has signed a three-year agreement with Phoenix to host SEMICON West.

title: Pegatron showcases rack-scale AI infrastructure at OCP Global Summit
snippet: Pegatron showcased its end-to-end AI infrastructure capabilities at the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit 2026, highlighting Nvidia-based products designed to move from engineering development to large-scale cluster deployment. The Taiwanese electronics manufacturer presented rack-scale AI systems, liquid-cooling technologies, and integrated deployment capabilities as demand grows for infrastructure that can support increasingly complex AI workloads.

title: KYEC signs advanced payment deal with Nvidia for US testing expansion
snippet: Taiwanese semiconductor testing services provider King Yuan Electronics (KYEC) is expanding its US footprint, with its board approving an advance payment agreement with Nvidia. title: AP Memory completes US$415.5M GDR offering, boosts three product lines
snippet: Memory IC design house AP Memory Technology has successfully priced its global depositary receipt (GDR) offering, raising a total of US$415.5 million. The GDRs were priced at US$56.15 per unit, representing approximately NT$897.61 per common share based on an exchange rate of NT$31.972 per US dollar. Scheduled to list on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange on October 15, the proceeds will be used to bolster working capital and satisfy foreign-currency raw material procurement needs.
